marks.gloss_en: all consecrated animals whose permanent blemish preceded their consecration, and which were redeemed, are obligated in the firstborn [law] and in the gifts
and one who slaughters them outside is exempt

and all whose consecration preceded their blemish, or [that had] a passing blemish before their consecration and afterwards a permanent blemish arose in them, and which were redeemed, are exempt from the firstborn [law] and from the gifts
and their offspring and their milk are forbidden after their redemption
טעמא דנפדו, הא לא נפדו -- from the mishna's 'and were redeemed': unredeemed, they are exempt
קסבר -- from the exemption of the unredeemed animal the stam reads the tanna's principle: sanctity of value pushes off from the firstborn and the gifts
the reason is that they were redeemed; but if they were not redeemed, they are exempt from the firstborn [law] and from the gifts
טעמא דנפדו, הא לא נפדו -- from the mishna's 'and were redeemed': unredeemed, they are forbidden in shearing and work
מסייע ליה לרבי אליעזר? -- the unredeemed animals' prohibition in shearing and work would support R' Eliezer
the reason is that they were redeemed; but if they were not redeemed, they are forbidden in shearing and work
אמרי: לא -- altar value-sanctity is confused with altar inherent sanctity, so the Rabbis decreed for it; Temple-maintenance sanctities -- no
דמיחלפא ... גזרו בהו רבנן -- the decree rests on the confusion
it is sanctity of value for the altar that is confused with inherent sanctity for the altar
הא לפני פדיונן אסירי -- from 'born after their redemption' in the mishna's case it follows that those born before redemption are forbidden
but [offspring born] before their redemption are forbidden
the mishna: their offspring and their milk are permitted after their redemption
